title: /api/ask was stateless, so FinAgent denied its own prior replies mid-conversation
example_quote: I don't have any earlier turn in this conversation where I provided Apple (or any other) quarterly numbers — this is the first message I'm seeing from you in this session.
fix_summary: Threaded real conversation history through the whole stack: /api/ask now accepts a `history` field, finagent.agent.graph.run_graph() replays it as HumanMessage/AIMessage turns before the new question (finagent.agent.moe_graph does the equivalent for the mixture-of-experts agent via a formatted prefix), every AgentRunner (FinAgentRunner, MoEAgentRunner, BedrockAgentRunner) forwards it, and web/app.js now maintains and sends the running conversation from the actual chat UI. The red-team tester itself was updated to send history the same way a real browser session does, so it now tests the product the way a user actually experiences it.
verification_note: A fresh live run (same 4 personas, same base app, history-aware tester) found 2 issues total, down from 8-11 in the two pre-fix runs, and zero were in the context-failure/self-contradiction category — across all 4 sessions, including Priya's persona which specifically pushes on cross-turn consistency. FinAgent correctly recalled and built on earlier turns throughout, at one point proactively cross-referencing itself: "consistent with the same forward-dated data issue you flagged earlier."
known_caveat: History is replayed as plain text only (no tool-call/tool-result blocks), so FinAgent can't always prove to itself that an earlier reply was tool-grounded. In one manual test, when pushed to re-verify a figure it had already correctly sourced from a tool, it re-called the tool (the right instinct) but mischaracterized its own earlier answer as "fabricated" when it hadn't been. Not part of this fix's scope; noted for a future pass.
